Theorem
[Higher interior regularity] 1. ch6:6.17\group gt-ch06 If $u\in C^2(\Omega )$ solves $Lu=f$ with coefficients and $f$ in $C^{k,\alpha }(\Omega )$, then $u\in C^{k+2,\alpha }(\Omega )$. Smooth data give $u\in C^\infty (\Omega )$.
Proof

\sketch Take difference quotients. For a coordinate direction and step $h$,

\begin{equation} \tag {6.49} L(\Delta _l^h u)=\Delta _l^h f-(\Delta _l^h a^{ij})D_{ij}u(\cdot +he_l) -(\Delta _l^h b^i)D_i u(\cdot +he_l)-(\Delta _l^h c)u(\cdot +he_l). \end{equation}

Interior estimates give uniform bounds and compactness; passing to $h\to 0$ proves the $k=1$ case. Differentiate repeatedly and induct.

□
